paper.title_en: Rotating black holes in perfect fluid dark matter: Horizons, photon orbits, and shadows
paper.abstract_en: We investigate rotating black holes surrounded by perfect-fluid dark matter (PFDM), described by the parameter k, and determine the Kerr-connected region of the (a/M, k/M) parameter space that contains an event horizon. The critical value kc(a), obtained from the degenerate-horizon conditions <math altimg="si22.svg"><mrow><mstyle mathvariant="normal"><mi>Δ</mi></mstyle><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><msup><mstyle mathvariant="normal"><mi>Δ</mi></mstyle><mo>′</mo></msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>, defines the boundary between black-hole and horizonless configurations. We derive an exact parametric form of this extremal boundary and show that its near-Kerr behavior includes a logarithmic correction; therefore, <math altimg="si23.svg"><mrow><msub><mi>k</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi></msub><mo linebreak="goodbreak">/</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>≃</mo><mn>2.8828</mn><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo linebreak="badbreak">−</mo><mi>a</mi><mo linebreak="badbreak">/</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><msup><mrow/><mrow><mn>1.5377</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> is only an empirical fit over 0.90 ≤ a/M ≤ 0.999, not an asymptotic scaling law. For horizon-bearing solutions, we calculate unstable spherical photon orbits and the shadow’s mean radius, area, and distortion, finding that increasing k/M shifts the photon region inward and reduces the shadow size. Backward ray tracing through a phenomenological optically thin disk, tested on independent 41<sup loc="post">2</sup>, 81<sup loc="post">2</sup>, and 161<sup loc="post">2</sup> image grids, confirms this trend: for <math altimg="si6.svg"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak">/</mo><mi>M</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mn>0.9</mn></mrow></math> and an inclination of 17<sup loc="post">∘</sup>, the 20 μas beam-convolved ridge diameter decreases from 42.47 to 37.88 μas as k/M increases from 0 to 0.08, with the two finest grids agreeing to within 0.5%. Thus, PFDM produces a consistent contraction from the horizon and photon region to the geometric shadow and image ridge, although these illustrative images do not provide an Event Horizon Telescope constraint because they lack a self-consistent emission model and interferometric likelihood analysis.
